A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AID research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST trainability experiments, image-classification generalizability experiments and DQN experiments on 17 Atari games, with additional analyses in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional generalizability controls, hyperparameter sensitivity results and Atari Dropout comparisons.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same interval-dependent masking, simplified Bernoulli selection between positive and negative ReLU, and deterministic test-time scaling. Appendix H implements this existing procedure; its newly disclosed rollout details do not establish a change to the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, TinyImageNet and the same 17 Atari games with the same task coverage. The new generalizability controls and sensitivity analyses reuse the existing continual-full datasets and setting.

E2.justification: The Atari comparisons gain a Dropout baseline: v1 Figure 6 compares vanilla DQN with AID, whereas v2 includes Dropout. Dropout also enters the per-game score and effective-rank comparisons in v2 Figures 14–15. The existing supervised comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Sections 3.1 and F.1.1 change reported subnetwork sampling from every epoch to every task, although Figure 2's caption still says epoch. Table 4 changes one S&P Adam learning rate from 1e-3 to 1e-4. New Appendix G.2 adds separately tuned reset/non-reset controls and a p-by-learning-rate sensitivity grid. These edits do not establish reruns of retained results.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing trainability and representation diagnostics, v2 adds controlled cold-start versus warm-start comparisons across all three image datasets and a systematic sensitivity analysis over four AID probabilities and two learning rates (G.2, Figures 10–11). It also extends the Atari effective-rank analysis to Dropout, substantially strengthening the supplementary investigation of plasticity.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five seeds generally and three for TinyImageNet/VGG-16 in F.6. Standard-deviation reporting and the Atari aggregate's stratified-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals are retained. The new sensitivity heatmaps use the existing mean-and-standard-deviation reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds generalizability-gap trajectories, sensitivity results and Dropout Atari score/rank series. For example, Figure 11 reports continual-full CIFAR10 accuracy of 60.86 ± 0.44% at p=0.6 and learning rate 0.001. These are additional results under specified conditions, rather than improvements to unchanged experiments; Table 1's existing numerical results remain identical.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1, Properties 1–3, Corollary C.1 and the derivations in Appendices A–D retain their mathematical substance. Equation numbering and notation change, while the expanded explanation of linearity regularization restates reasoning already present in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal introduction/conclusion claims remain the same: AID regularizes toward linear-network behavior, is compatible with He initialization, and preserves plasticity across supervised and reinforcement-learning settings. Additional evidence supports these retained contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the interpretation of 10.9, 10.1 and 3.3 percentage points as vanilla, Dropout and AID cold/warm accuracy gaps. The RL discussion newly attributes modest Dropout gains to ensembling. The conclusion explicitly acknowledges that the theory's relationship to improved generalizability remains uncertain, and Appendix H discusses instability from stochastic rollouts.

D1.justification: New Appendix H supplies a PyTorch implementation and discloses using evaluation mode for greedy action selection during RL rollouts for both Dropout and AID. Tables 3 and 9 add Dropout's RL search range and per-game selections. These improve implementation documentation without establishing changes to previously used procedures.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ma et al. (2023) and an introduction passage connecting data augmentation, overfitting and plasticity loss. The broader positioning is retained; several other reference edits update metadata for works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The revision makes targeted explanatory rewrites, standardizes terminology and labels such as DIA/AID and Concat ReLU/CReLU, updates affiliations and adds acknowledgements. New generalizability and implementation appendix sections expand the document while preserving its main narrative structure.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands through the new multi-panel generalizability comparison and sensitivity heatmaps in Figures 10–11. RL figures gain Dropout curves and legends, Table 9 gains a Dropout column, and Appendix H adds a code listing. Further changes include Figure 7 axis adjustments, table formatting and relocation of Algorithm 2 and Figure 5; the renumbered class-incremental plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The matched reset/non-reset comparisons and Atari Dropout baseline strengthen the empirical support, while Appendix H improves reproducibility and the conclusion better qualifies the theory's scope. These are useful incremental gains over v1's already extensive experiments and retained theoretical results. The remaining epoch/task mismatch in Figure 2's caption limits protocol clarity but does not outweigh the additions.
